slides.text: AI News Gemini 4 Argon - Google's Latest Frontier AI Model Ouputs up to 1 Mln tokens in one answer (up from 64K) Input Context Window not disclosed yet Targets complex, extended work in coding, business knowledge tasks, legal, finance, cybersecurity defense. Initial access limited to cyber defenders and testers Argon handles demanding, multi-step tasks that require sustained reasoning and execution https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/ https://ai-tldr.dev/models/google-gemini-4-argon/ Introductory price $2/$10 per million tokens, later $4/$20 Google's RRSI lets agents rewrite their own harness RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses The agent edits its own prompts, tools, memory, control flow and sub-agents; model weights never change Regularized so the harness does not just memorize its training tasks From Google Cloud AI Research with UNC, Stanford and WashU Open source under Apache 2.0; works with any LiteLLM model https://github.com/google-research/rrsi

It tends to lead with the main point and explain complex ideas with less jargon. That style may make it better for summarizing architecture discussions, including decisions, alternatives, and tradeoffs Note that clarity does not guarantee greater accuracy Anthropic also reports stronger performance on complex coding tasks, faster output, and lower API prices than Opus 5 Its summaries may not always be shorter: one analysis found Opus 5.5’s responses were somewhat longer on average Recent Claude Opus Versions Release Dates and Training Data Cutoff 4.5  Nov 24, 2025 / - 4.6  Feb  5, 2026 / Aug 2025 - very good 4.7  Apr 16, 2026 / Jan 2026 - 4.8  May 28, 2026 / Jan 2026 - worse 5.0  Jul 24, 2026 / May 2026 - worse 5.5  Sep 22, 2026 / -        - very good Claude Marketplace opens with 2,000+ connectors and plugins 2,000+ MCP connectors and plugins, including Google, Microsoft, Notion, Salesforce Claude-powered agents from Cursor, CrowdStrike and Snowflake Consulting partners such as Accenture and Deloitte Builders can list their own tools and agents https://claude.com/blog/claude-marketplace

slides.title: DeepSeek DSec paper AI Agents Train Their Successors
slides.text: DeepSeek DSec paper AI Agents Train Their Successors DeepSeek DSec paper - 130-plus authors https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22978 DSec (DeepSeek Elastic Compute) is DeepSeek’s infrastructure for running AI agents in isolated, disposable sandboxes DSec provides isolated practice computers where agents can write and test code without risking production systems. A cluster handles about 3 million sandboxes daily, with more than 380K  running simultaneously Its layered, on-demand environments reduce startup time, storage writes, and memory use, while letting agents assemble reusable training environments themselves. That approach addresses a key constraint in RSI (Recursive Self-Improvement) - producing enough reliable tasks and environments, not just adding GPUs The cluster reports creation of more than 5K sandboxes per sec The main speedup comes from avoiding full image downloads DSec stores environment images in DeepSeek’s 3FS distributed file system and loads only the data blocks an agent actually accesses. Uses EROFS (Enhanced Read-Only File System) for speed https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=63nU3-EXf6g DSec Scales Sandboxes for Agentic RL Training Problem: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) needs many reliable, stateful task environments; the speed of provisioning and resource use can limit training throughput Solution: DSec combines function-call, container, microVM, and full-VM sandboxes, loading image data on demand instead of downloading complete images Achievement: DeepSeek reports over 5,000 sandbox creations per second, about 3 million daily, and more than 380,000 simultaneous sandboxes. Importance: It demonstrates that environment capacity - not GPUs alone - can constrain agent training. Similar sandbox concepts are used by all major AI training vendors

slides.title: DHH Keynote DHH (David Heinemeier Hansson) Keynote Rails
slides.text: DHH Keynote DHH (David Heinemeier Hansson) Keynote Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vDjW_dRyKXY DHH is a Danish programmer and entrepreneur, and the creator of Ruby on Rails He is a co-owner and CTO of 37signals ( https://37signals.com ) - the company behind Basecamp and HEY. He is also an author and is known as a race-car driver. DHH opens Rails World 2026 in Austin with a keynote on the age of AI agents: why 37signals has gone "pencils down" - stopping hand-written coding, why Rails' convention over configuration is built for this moment, and why the only play left is total optimism The speaker sees AI agents as a major turning point in computing, comparable to photography becoming widely accessible. As implementation costs fall, developers can build more software and focus on outcomes rather than hand-writing code AI is changing programming roles, workflows, and architecture. Teams should delegate tasks to agents, review results, and rethink practices designed for human-written code Some products may shift from web apps to native apps as multi-platform development becomes cheaper, while the web remains useful for easy, installation-free access Agents can also help create efficient backends, search by meaning, and customize computing environments Developers should build agent-friendly interfaces, such as command-line tools, and address security risks through engineering The speaker’s message is optimistic: hand-coding had a valuable era, but the future belongs to people who guide AI to make useful things

slides.title: JEV - page 1 When to Use JEV
slides.text: JEV - page 1 When to Use JEV JEV is a TypeSafe AI’s decision model Its strongest use cases are workflows that need a fast, repeatable, machine-readable judgment from a known set of possible answers - not a conversational response Jev returns probabilities of typed choices, scores, or yes/no (“Noul” questions), so your application can use the result directly in its control flow. https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python - python API Use case Example Classification and triage Sort support tickets by topic or urgency, categorize emails, or flag items for human review. Routing Choose the right team, workflow, tool, or AI model for an incoming request. Content moderation Check for spam or policy violations, then route uncertain cases to moderators. Scoring and ranking Prioritize leads, rank candidate items, or score reviews against a defined rubric. Agent guardrails Assess whether a proposed tool call or action meets a risk rule before your system executes it. Verification checks Estimate whether a specific claim or condition is true, or whether an item meets a checklist. Real-time decisions Make frequent choices in interactive systems / games Laya by ConvAI Innovations - better than Jev by Nandakishor Mukkunnoth, open-weight model Classification, scoring, or yes/no Apache 2.0 alternative to Jev, can run locally Privacy, ownership, tuning/customization, speed Speed and benchmark wins are not independently settled; one comparison found Jev more accurate before adapting Laya to its test data Based on ModernBERT-large (or mmBERT-base) model, trained using RLCD (Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions) https://anth.us/blog/jev-vs-laya/ https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya Fastino GLiDE - Jev-like model, via API Fastino is in San Francisco, CA Fastino GLiDE is better than Jev on 31 of 38 benchmarks. https://fastino.ai GLiNER2.5-Decide - open-weight decision model https://huggingface.co/fastino/GLiNER2.5-Decide

slides.title: JEV - page 2 Contrastive Language Models score
slides.text: JEV - page 2 Contrastive Language Models score agent, 9x faster than Jev Stanford and NVIDIA released CLM-8B , an open System One model It scores candidate actions and returns probabilities Two small heads on a frozen Qwen3-8B, trained with a contrastive loss Matches Jev on computer use, games and tool calling, x9 times faster As a fine-tuned verifier: 81.6% on DeepSWE, 87.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 https://huggingface.co/Contrastive-LM/CLM-v0.1-8B https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eSuMmMMMrm0 Jeff - Classifier for Under $5 Fine-tuned Qwen3.5 4B with LoRA to classify supplied text against listed choices and return a compact decision Trained on public classification datasets, routing, and research examples; trained and served the model using Modal, Unsloth, and vLLM Trained on L40S GPU and deploying inference on L40S and H100 GPUs Training cost $4.17, training time 2 hours Held-out evaluation reached 88% accuracy Warm responses were generally subsecond https://github.com/SonDaoRM/Jef-qwen3.5-4b-finetune-banking77 https://github.com/togethercomputer/tev1 https://www.together.ai/blog/how-to-train-your-own-jev OpenRouter launches Jev Router to pick a model for each request typesafe/jev-router - powered by the Jev decision model Before the LLM call, it picks the model and the reasoning effort It weighs quality, speed and cost, and knows what is cached Solved 82% more tasks than OpenRouter's Auto Router on four agent benchmarks (237 vs 130 of 423) Accepts up to 1M tokens; the router itself is listed at $0 https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-router

slides.title: JEV - page 3 Modal's Quail processes a
slides.text: JEV - page 3 Modal's Quail processes a Billion tokens per minute on one H100 Quail (Query-Aware Inference Layer) runs LLM calls inside SQL queries, such as AI filters and joins Over 1B-tokens/min per H100 1.84x faster than vLLM on average , more than 10x on multi-join queries Under 6 cents per Billion tokens on Prefill only: a yes/no classification needs a single output token SELECT r.id FROM reviews r WHERE AI.IF(PROMPT('Does this review discuss the ending?\n\n{0}', r.body)) Modal Labs, Inc. is a New York City based cloud-computing platform for AI developers. Since 2021, ~150 people. Raised $466M+, $4.65B valuation https://modal.com/blog/quail-billion-tpm https://github.com/fsdatalab/quail - open source Ollama Adds Local Jev-like Decision Models Integrating TypeSafe’s Jev-style decision API, with models from Bespoke Labs and Together AI Ollama v. 0.35 adds the `/v1/systemone` endpoint , which answers multiple typed decision questions in one request ollama pull nimble Local decision models offer fast & free decisions Three models are available - Nimble 9B, Tev1 4B, and Tev1 0.8B Nimble gives same accuracy as Jev - but averaged 91 ms per decision in a local Pac-Man example. Other examples - highly  responsive ticket triage, model routing, and moderation. https://ollama.com/blog/ollama-now-supports-jev-style-decision-models

slides.title: Ethernet , Internet May 22, 1973, Robert Metcalfe
slides.text: Ethernet , Internet May 22, 1973, Robert Metcalfe proposed “Ethernet” in a memo at Xerox PARC in California. It is a combination of “ether” ( a supposed all-pervading medium for waves) with “net” meaning network Metcalfe used “ether” as a metaphor for the shared cable medium carrying computer transmissions 1974, Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn developed and described protocols for linking separate packet networks. “Internet” appeared in RFC 675, published in December 1974, as shorthand for “internetwork” or “internetworking.” Word "Internet" described interconnected networks communicating through common protocols https://www.computerhistory.org/tdih/may/22/ https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc675/ https://www.scienceandmediamuseum.org.uk/objects-and-stories/short-history-internet

slides.title: AI News NVIDIA puts an AI agent watchdog
slides.text: AI News NVIDIA puts an AI agent watchdog into silicon Nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform Guards agents at two layers:  host CPU and DPU OpenShell - open-source (Apache 2.0) runtime that sandboxes agents with kernel-level isolation Policies set what an agent may touch in files, network, processes and inference Sentry runs out of band on BlueField-4 DPUs and quarantines a rule-breaking agent in milliseconds A compromised agent runtime cannot reach or disable the watchdog 100+ partners at launch, including Anthropic, Microsoft, CrowdStrike, SAP and JPMorganChase https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/open-agent-safety-platform https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/openshell/ - OpenShell AMD to Acquire Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at about $8.2 Bln Expected to close by the end of 2026 World Labs develops AI “world models” that can understand, generate, and simulate 3D environments AMD says the acquisition will bring in research talent to help shape its AI hardware, software, and systems for emerging workloads such as robotics and physical AI

slides.title: AI News Fireworks.AI Ember-1 - 40% less Tokens
slides.text: AI News Fireworks.AI Ember-1 - 40% less Tokens Ember-1 is a Fireworks Research post-trained version of Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 Its aim is to preserve K3’s task quality while generating substantially shorter reasoning traces Kimi K3 is the underlying 2.8-Trillion-parameter model Results: 71% fewer reasoning tokens, 39% fewer in total, same success rate Same per-token price as K3, 1M-token context Status: Research Preview on the Fireworks serverless API only; no weights Fireworks AI, Inc. - a startup in California . It was founded in 2022 by Lin Qiao and other former Meta/PyTorch engineers. Size - approx 200 people. It has grown into a major AI-infrastructure company: in July 2026 it raised about $1.5 Bln in Series D funding at a reported $17.5 Bln valuation https://fireworks.ai/blog/ember-1 https://fireworks.ai

slides.text: AI News Cloudflare and AWS - open Jev-style decision models the same day Cloudflare Clef (27B) and Clef-flash (9B) return typed probabilities instead of text Median latency 209 ms and 39 ms, against 524 ms for TypeSafe's Jev BANKING77: 94.20 macro-F1 for Clef vs 79.74 for Jev; fully Jev-API compatible Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face, 64K context, also reads images AWS Strands Decider 2B picks options in about 115 ms on one RTX 3090 Apache 2.0 with code and training recipe: pip install strands-decider https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/ Claude Code mods - Customize the Agent TypeScript/Javascript plugins that change the agent Mods hook into every tool call, turn and screen redraw, and can observe, rewrite or answer them Blast Radius - preview risky deletions. Pauses rm -rf , hard resets and force pushes and shows what they would touch Token Weather - shows context use and a sparkline of the last 12 turns Replay Theater - lets you step through every edit Claude made Built-in /diff is itself a mod; works in the CLI and desktop Code tab Mods get the agent's full access to your machine, so install only trusted ones You can describe a desired mod to Claude Code, which can create, install, and reload it Plugins are managed through `/plugin` . https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-mods
